struck: R3 allows buildings up to 55 feet on lots as small as 3,600 square feet.
use: R3 allows buildings up to 55 feet, and a detached house on a lot of 3,600 square feet (3,000 for an attached house).

pattern: (one|single|unbroken) band[^.]{0,120}(north|town line)|from the north town line to the south town line
struck: R3 and C3 form one band along the ocean, from the north town line to the south town line.
use: R3 and C3 run along the ocean the length of the town, broken at the pier by the C4 district.

struck: R1 and R2 fill the streets inland of it to the commercial strip on US 17.
use: R1 and R2 cover most of the streets between them and the commercial strip on US 17 Business.

struck: In R3 about 1 home in 8 is someone's main home.
use: In R3 about 1 home in 8 is taxed as its owner's main home.

struck: The town uses the county assessor's building value, land excluded.
use: The town uses the county assessor's building value, land excluded, unless the owner submits a licensed appraisal.

struck: A flood policy on a single-family home costs a middle $1,256 a year in the block group nearest the ocean.
use: In the census block group from the south town line to the pier, a single-family flood policy costs a middle $1,256 a year.

struck: The council debate was over running carts 24 hours a day, and the ordinance passed 5 to 2.
use: The town council passed golf cart Ordinance 25-0990 on August 26, 2025, by 5 votes to 2; speakers at the meeting argued for and against a 24-hour rule.

struck: Beach wheelchairs are lent by the town police.
use: Beach wheelchairs are available through the town police department.

struck: The land was the Ark Plantation of John Tillman; it was later Floral Beach, for George J. Holiday's wife Flora and daughter Floramay.
use: Much of its land was once the Ark Plantation; the beach was later called Roach's Beach, then Floral Beach, and took the name Surfside Beach in 1952.

struck: In a hurricane evacuation, everything in the town east of Highway 17 is in Zone A and everything west of it is in Zone B.
use: Near the ocean the town is in hurricane evacuation Zone A; part of it east of US 17 Business, from 16th Avenue North to Vista Drive, is in Zone B.

struck: Yearly cost line for the typical inland house lived in: its town and county tax as a main home is about $2,050 a year.
use: A buyer of an inland R1 house the county values at about $488,000 (the middle R1 house) pays about $2,050 a year in town and county tax as a main home, before credits.

struck: South of the pier, it follows Willow Drive South for a few blocks. Then it runs just behind the houses on Lakeside Drive, which are on the rental side. (Map titles: south of the pier it runs behind Lakeside Drive.)
use: South of the pier, it follows Willow Drive South for about 0.3 mile, to about 6th Avenue South. From there it follows Lakeside Drive: houses on the ocean side of Lakeside are on the rental side, and houses on its inland side are not.

struck: A house near the ocean, rented or a second home, costs about $12,300 a year besides the mortgage and home insurance, with a flood policy of about $1,250.
use: A house near the ocean, rented or a second home, costs about $12,400 a year besides the mortgage and home insurance, with a flood policy of about $1,350.

struck: A free concert in Memorial Park, next to the library, every Sunday evening.
use: A free concert in Memorial Park, next to the library, on Sundays from 4 to 7 p.m.
